Thunderbird is software installed on you computer, so the only person with access to your copy is you and anyone you give access to the physical device. So there is no Are you having problems with the program right now?" this is not like a website which might be down.

So moving to your actual issue. Removing an account removes any emails it contains on your local machine. re adding an account can in some cases download mail that is on the mail server, but not always. It is not cut and dried.

Then we have

Also, sending messages has slowed way way down or refused to send.

I think this indicates issues that have little of nothing to do with Thunderbird and everything to do with other software you have installed like an antivirus product.

So;

  1. what mail provider are we taking about mail from?
  2. What was the issue that prompted the removal of your account that had the mail in it? I rather doubt what you have done has done more than moved the visible problem
  3. Is the account configured in Thunderbird as IMAP or POP? or is is it the more experimental exchange type of account?
